questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: New culture, change of scenery, new people. Academic challenges also spoke to me, since a lot of great professors are at the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The only thing being less than 10/10 is the university experience. There was barely any assistance on figuring out the university and no introduction or help to find the right classroom on the first day for example. I wasn't paired with any mentor or student of NYU, so I was completely on my own. Some people might prefer this, but I found it hard to figure out how to approach social life at NYU the best. Turns out there isn't that much social life at NYU outside the dorm-life. Would have been nice with more guidance in general as well as when electing courses. I ended up not getting any of the eight courses that was on my wish list.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it tricky but researching the digital platforms of NYU made it easier.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None. You have to ask for assistance if you need it and it is quite hard to figure out which office is the right one for assisting you.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Orientation and assistance upon arrival was the poorest thing about my stay since there wasn't any.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is expensive to live in New York. I lived in The Academic Guest House of Bikubenfonden. This is a place that works like a scholarship, since you do not actually pay rent. You just have to pay for utilities and services. This means it is cheap to live there, yet it is a super nice place on the Upper West Side. Would definitely recommend applying. The application process is a bit cumbersome, but worth it! You live with all Danes.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive in New York if you do not get in to Bikuben. Try to talk to people in the facebook-group "Danes in New York" and see if you can find someone to get a place with. Then you don't have to stay in a tiny room in Brooklyn.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Ended up not getting any of the courses that I requested so the experience was a bit poor for me.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to pick a course and then send your prerequisites from UCPH to NYU in order for them to approve of you since you don't have any prerequisities in their system. This makes the process very slow and for me resulted in all the courses I wanted filling up before I got approved.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is an office at NYU that can help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be early and be very pro-active.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 4th year undergraduate courses at NYU, since their masters programme is at PhD-level and so they don't let in exchange students. The academic level wasn't that high, but I though it was nice to be able to take breaks and experience the city during my stay.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Advanced Macroeconomics, advanced econometrics, public economics, labor economics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are a bachelor's student I would recommend public economics. If you want something a bit harder I would recommend advanced macroeconomics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Medical costs, where insurance didn't cover as much as I had expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is expensive. Even just cooking at home is expensive. So remember to take account of groceries being more expensive than DK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really participate in any, so I don't know. Participated in a book club that was interesting and they have great sports facilities if you want to go for a swim for example.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You have to really seek it out.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Maybe be more pro-active than me in seeking out clubs and social events.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is an endless list of things to do in New York. So much amazing food and great locations to have a beer.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be pro-active and approach people because they most likely will not approach you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Weed is legal in New York and everyone smokes.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Apply for financial aid through danish foundations. Find a nice place to stay (Bikuben). Be pro-active in course-selection.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Seek out the offices at NYU if you need help. They do not actively help you if you do not ask for help, but they have a lot of valuable information.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The culture and the city. Living in such a diverse city for 5 months.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The administrative work with selecting courses, doing taxes and figuring out insurance to pay medical bills.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
